analysis: Examined head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 55091-56732). The file is a public golden-vector fixture for the prompt contract: request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries, chain hashes) and token_ids. All content is synthetic ('Public followup', 'Public synthetic cache-parity input', 'Nulls must disappear'), with no secrets, credentials, keys, tokens or real consumer data. The patch excerpt shows template_input gaining additional_context.enable_thinking=false in some vectors, with changed prompt_token_count, chain hashes and token_ids; the visible reasoning_effort vector already carries additional_context. These are test-fixture changes that track the template and tokenizer behavior. They touch no authorization, attestation, encryption, routing or billing code. Relevant model areas are T-041 (prefix-cache chain hashes and cross-tenant sharing) and TB-007. The fixtures only define expected hash and token outputs, so a wrong value would show up as a parity-test failure rather than a runtime security control change. Remaining integration questions, outside the supplied evidence: whether the Swift and Go implementations that consume these vectors were updated consistently, including prompt_contract_id and the enable_thinking default. A mismatch would cause cache-key or availability issues rather than disclosure. The patch excerpt is truncated and the other changed ranges (for example around lines 3805-3926, 4752 and 43739) were not visible, so I cannot rule out other fixture changes. No concrete security regression is identified.
